↳ Posted by DaveF on May 1st, 2022.

Different-sounding Lake District version of this tune?

I’ve just come across a tune by this title (“Round the World for Sport”) in John Offord’s book “Bonny Cumberland: Music from the manuscripts of fiddlers in the Lake District c. 1750-1880” (pg. 28), and the tune as transcribed there sounds decidedly different -- more Border country or Scottish in rhythm, and not really at all like the versions posted here.

I’m not good at ABC notation but will attempt to transcribe it here. I think this Lake District version is in E-Dorian but I’m not totally sure. Cut time, two sharps:

M: 2/2
K: E Dorian

E(F/G/) AB AGAB | GG/G/ BA G2 E2 | FGGB AGAB | B(c/d/) Ad FD D2 :|
geef gbeg | fddg f(g/a/) fd | geef gbed | BdAB GE E2 | geef gbeg | f(g/a/) fd | gbfa efdA BdAF E2 E2

There’s a note with this tune that it was edited by Chris Partington, with BF 14.02 written beside it, which looks to be a manuscript reference to an old fiddler’s tunebook collection (http://www.cpartington.plus.com/Links/Browne/Browne%20Info.html)

At that link, you can view a PDF of his transcription from that old manuscript, including the unedited version of this tune next to the edited version.

Does anyone know anything about the history of this Lake District tune? Is it possibly related to the other versions of the tune with this name posted here, or is it just coincidental that they share a name?

(It does have a distant similarity to the Three Merry Sisters of Fate that Dr. Dow linked to above (tune #4331), but more in the rhythm and some of the string crossings.)

Thanks for any insights!
